name: Ethylhexyl triazone
lead: Ethylhexyl triazone (octyl triazone, EHT; Uvinul T 150 from BASF, Parsol EHT from DSM-Firmenich) is an oil-soluble organic UVB filter with an absorption maximum near 314 nm. Its structure is a triazine ring bearing three 2-ethylhexyl benzoate groups.[1][2]

Grokipedia describes it as highly photostable and used at low concentrations to raise SPF, and says it is permitted in the EU at up to 5% but lacks US approval as a sunscreen active.[2] Its Wikipedia article is a short stub with no history or safety data.[1]
Published research on EHT is mostly analytical, environmental and formulation work. No clinical trial of ethylhexyl triazone alone was found.
infobox: Not an approved sunscreen active (per Grokipedia)

paras: EHT is used in sunscreens, creams, sprays and makeup, usually with other filters such as avobenzone.[2] A US drug label shows it combined with bisoctrizole, diethylhexyl butamido triazone and DHHB in one product.[3] Studies have examined organic filters in lipid nanoparticle formulations,[4] with ferulic acid to improve SPF and UVA protection factor,[5] and in tests comparing fifteen sunscreen products of equal label SPF under natural sunlight.[6]

Researchers have studied how filters photostabilise one another and quench triplet states in combination.[7] Percutaneous penetration of sunscreen filters has been measured in vitro with HPLC methods.[8]

A UK multicentre photopatch study of 1155 patients examined sunscreen chemicals as photoallergens, noting they are among the most common photoallergens in the UK.[9] A multi-centre European photopatch study is also registered.[10]

Filters of this type have been measured in wastewater and sewage sludge, with fate and removal studied across treatment plants,[11][12] in European sea sediment,[13] and in a toxicity test on brine shrimp and algae.[14]
No studies found for ethylhexyl triazone itself. Related human research covers sunscreens and photoallergens as a group.[9][10]

card.summary: A highly photostable UVB filter used in high-SPF products abroad; no clinical trials of it alone.
card.aka: Octyl triazone, EHT, Uvinul T 150, Parsol EHT
card.note: Not an approved US sunscreen active, per Grokipedia.

quick.overview:
Ethylhexyl triazone is an oil-soluble sunscreen ingredient that absorbs UVB light. It is used in products in the EU and elsewhere to help reach high SPF values.

Sources are thin: no clinical trials of it alone were found.
quick.mechanism: It absorbs UVB near 314 nm and dissipates the energy as heat; it is typically combined with UVA filters.
quick.risks: Sunscreen filters as a class are recognised photoallergens in dermatology clinics. Environmental studies have measured similar filters in wastewater, sludge and sediment.
